research_question: During continuous finite-area probe contact with soft and heterogeneous environments, under which measurable combinations of contact-history timescale, local geometry or contact-area change, sliding rate, and material shift does a scalar memoryless force-indentation/rate representation cease to be decision-equivalent to a stateful contact representation for selecting robot impedance, as judged by held-out impedance actions, force or wrench safety outcomes, and scanning-task outcomes?
observed_phenomenon: The evidence shows a structured contradiction rather than a simple missing model: memory and creep can change force, pressure distribution, contact area, and tangential-moment capacity; low-order viscoelastic identification can improve calibrated tissue force control; finite-area Hertz or PFC models can improve tracking or reproduce area-dependent wrench; yet contact-model-agnostic admittance and static-output GP-MPC can already achieve accurate nominal force regulation or enforce conditional force constraints. What remains unmeasured is when richer contact state changes the impedance decision and the closed-loop outcome, rather than merely improving open-loop fit.
scope_and_conditions: Continuous sliding or scanning by a rigid probe over compliant, finite-area environments, centered on robotic ultrasound-like contact and bounded to contact regimes with measurable force or wrench, indentation or pose, speed, contact history, and task-quality signals. Comparisons must include nominally matched memoryless HC-like force-depth/rate, finite-area memoryless, contact-model-agnostic feedback, and stateful low-order memory representations; train or calibrate on one subset and test on held-out material, curvature, speed, direction, dwell history, and disturbance conditions. The question excludes claims about all soft-body dynamics, clinical efficacy, and universal tissue injury thresholds.
why_it_matters: The answer determines whether contact-model complexity is a necessary scientific carrier for safe and effective optimal impedance or an unnecessary identification burden. A regime map and minimal-sufficiency result would transfer across robotic scanning and other continuous compliant-contact tasks, prevent novelty claims already exhausted by viscoelastic force control, contact-aware MPC, PFC, or learned force models, and identify which safety and task claims can actually be supported under model shift.
value_if_yes: If a reproducible boundary exists, it yields a falsifiable rule for when contact history or finite-area state must enter impedance selection, identifies the smallest control-relevant state, and enables targeted safety or task guarantees specifically in regimes where simpler models are not decision-equivalent.
value_if_no: If calibrated memoryless or contact-model-agnostic baselines remain decision-equivalent within prespecified margins across held-out shifts, the richer model is scientifically unnecessary for this task class; effort should shift to robust feedback, uncertainty calibration, constraint design, and sensing rather than adding constitutive states.

plausible_explanations.explanation: A low-dimensional relaxation and evolving-contact-area state becomes action-relevant when the environment timescale is comparable to dwell or sliding timescale, because identical instantaneous force, indentation, and velocity can imply different future wrench capacity and therefore different impedance choices.

Robust measured-wrench feedback or calibrated static-output uncertainty absorbs most model mismatch, so richer constitutive state improves prediction but does not materially change optimal gains or closed-loop outcomes.

Reported benefits of richer models arise mainly from offline calibration, sensor delay, friction or coupling-medium changes, geometry registration, or comparator weakness rather than material memory itself.
Detailed material or pressure parameters are too weakly identifiable during safe excitation, and only a smaller latent sufficient statistic—or no additional state—is reproducibly useful for control.

measurement_validity: Use synchronized, independently calibrated six-axis wrench, robot pose or indentation, commanded and rendered impedance, sliding speed, and an independent task-quality signal such as image confidence or reconstruction consistency. Separate identification and held-out evaluation specimens or regions; repeat conditions in randomized order; report transient and steady endpoints with uncertainty; verify sensor bandwidth and delay; and test whether state estimates are observable and stable before attributing outcome differences to contact memory.
artifact_or_confound_alternatives: Force or torque sensor drift, filtering, latency, saturation, or gravity-compensation error
Coupling-gel thickness, lubrication, drying, temperature, hydration, or specimen aging
Robot structural compliance, low-level tracking error, solver horizon, saturation, or optimizer failure
Surface curvature or normal-direction registration error misattributed to material heterogeneity
Estimator leakage from test trajectories or unequal calibration data and compute budgets
Image-confidence miscalibration, perception-network shift, or reconstruction error unrelated to contact control
Frictional stick-slip, adhesion, or contact loss mistaken for viscoelastic relaxation
independent_support: Ubx3Xkv4y2kJ analytically links viscoelastic history to evolving finite-area wrench capacity under two loading modes.
iasK6kEBzIEJ and _8NXx8-VkcgJ independently show low-order viscoelastic models can matter in tissue force transients but remain calibration-bound.
QPuQ4sfxSTIJ and ZDySGaNsMn8J show geometry-aware soft-contact models can improve model-predictive tracking in separate manipulation settings.

USER-TUFFC-2011-1961 independently shows finite-thickness memory identification can be nonunique, constraining claims about recoverable state.
phenomenon_prevalence_or_effect_scale: Time dependence, finite contact area, and model mismatch are documented across tissue indentation, robotic tissue force control, compliant grasping, ultrasound scanning, and force-motion MPC, but their prevalence and effect size specifically for continuous optimal-impedance scanning are not yet quantified. Reported adjacent effects range from missed force-decay trends and unstable or constraint-violating baselines to substantial model or tracking-error reductions; these heterogeneous results motivate measuring a regime boundary rather than assuming universal benefit.
decision_owner_and_threshold: The scientific decision owner is the problem-quality and novelty review sequence, followed by the human problem Gate. Experimentally, a stateful representation is deemed necessary only if, under matched data, computation, controller objective, and safety constraints, it changes selected stiffness or damping beyond implementation resolution and produces a repeatable held-out improvement whose confidence interval exceeds a prespecified sensor- and task-relevant equivalence margin on at least one primary safety or task endpoint without a material loss on the others. Otherwise the simpler representation is accepted as decision-equivalent for that regime.
falsifier: Across the declared held-out material, geometry, speed, direction, dwell-history, and disturbance conditions, a calibrated scalar memoryless HC-like model or contact-model-agnostic uncertainty-aware baseline selects impedance actions within the prespecified equivalence margin and matches the stateful representation on transient force or wrench, constraint violations, contact loss or slip, and independent scanning-task quality; additionally, inferred memory or contact-area states fail observability, cross-trial reproducibility, or incremental prediction tests.
feasible_discriminating_probe: Run a bounded repeated-measures benchtop study using several soft phantoms spanning relaxation times and stiffness, at least two curvatures or thicknesses, randomized sliding speeds and dwell histories, and withheld regions or specimens. Under one common impedance-selection objective and matched compute/data budgets, compare contact-model-agnostic feedback, scalar HC-like force-depth/rate, finite-area memoryless, and low-order stateful representations. First test one-step and horizon prediction plus state observability; then compare selected impedance trajectories and predeclared transient force, wrench, contact-loss or slip, and image-quality endpoints. A small ex-vivo confirmation may test transfer without making a clinical claim.
closest_prior_answer: NNBO already combines HC with learned optimal impedance for a nominal soft environment; AuSoScan embeds a calibrated velocity-dependent Hertz contact law in robotic-ultrasound MPC; deformable-contact-aware MPC incorporates local contact geometry and friction; generalized-Maxwell tissue identification already supports offline force-controller tuning; velocity-level PFC is already real-time; and hybrid GP-MPC already tightens force constraints under static-output uncertainty. None of these decision-grade priors tests whether contact history or evolving finite-area state is minimally necessary for impedance selection under held-out continuous soft-contact shifts, nor whether simpler feedback or uncertainty-aware control is decision-equivalent.
uncertainties: Which dimensionless ratio of relaxation, dwell, and sliding timescales best predicts the boundary
Whether contact area or pressure can be measured or inferred safely and at sufficient bandwidth
Whether impedance-action differences remain after equalizing controller objectives, data, and compute
Which independent scanning-quality endpoint is reliable enough for a primary outcome
How far phantom regime boundaries transfer to ex-vivo or in-vivo tissue
What equivalence margins are justified by sensor resolution and task or safety relevance
Whether finite-area tangential or moment effects are material for the chosen probe geometry
